title: 2026 MLS Cup Playoffs: Bracket, Schedule, Key Matches and Route to Glory
subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Zach LowyNov 7, 2026The playoffs begin later this month. / Erica Denhoff/NurPhoto/Getty Images (left); Griffin C. Hooper/Getty Images (top right); Chris Arjoon/Icon Sportswire/Getty Images (bottom right)The 2026 MLS regular season has come and gone, with 12 teams saying goodbye to their campaigns and 18 set to return to action after the November international break. The attention now turns to the MLS Cup playoffs, and it’s fair to say that there are quite a few intriguing match-ups.

In the East, Nashville SC await the winner of the wild-card match, which will pit Orlando City against FC Cincinnati, while defending champions Inter Miami will take on the most in-form team in MLS at the minute, Columbus Crew. New England Revolution will lock horns with Philadelphia Union in a battle of rising USMNT stars.

In the West, Seattle Sounders will host the wild card match against Real Salt Lake, with the winner set to face Vancouver Whitecaps. Meanwhile, San Jose Earthquakes will take on Houston Dynamo in the first round—a match no one can predict.
Here’s everything to know about the upcoming MLS Cup playoffs, including the full bracket and schedule.

Following the wild card games on Nov. 19, the Round One best-of-three matchups will take place between Nov. 20 and Dec. 2, with the higher-ranked side hosting the first and third matches (if necessary).
The conference semifinals is set for Dec. 5. and Dec. 6, with the conference finals on Dec. 11 and Dec. 12. The highly anticipated MLS Cup final will take place on Dec. 18.

This will be the final MLS Cup playoffs played in winter, with the league switching to a fall-to-spring format in 2027 to better align with the European calendar. Ultimately, this will come down to which teams can prevail in the chilly conditions and which players will have ice in their veins.

Inter Miami have a tall task as they seek to avoid an opening-round elimination. / Megan Briggs/Getty ImagesEver since Lionel Messi landed in South Florida, Inter Miami have won a major trophy: the Leagues Cup (2023), the Supporters’ Shield (2024) and the MLS Cup (2025). But if they are to continue that streak and achieve the first successful title defense since LA Galaxy in 2011–12, they’ll have to go through the hottest team in MLS first.

In just over two months, Columbus Crew have gone from sitting at the bottom of the East to finishing seventh. They've won six on the bounce (scoring 3+ in four of those), and there's every reason to believe that they can make life difficult for a Miami side that has struggled for consistency this year.

Inter Miami, meanwhile, are leaking goals at the moment. They’ve conceded at least two goals in five of their last 10 matches, and even when they looked destined for a comfortable 3–0 win on Decision Day, they conceded three straight goals to Charlotte FC. The Herons are struggling to convince at the back, and Columbus could punish their defensive frailties and come away with the upset win.
OH MY BRAIS MÉNDEZ!As it stands, @ColumbusCrew would avoid the Wildcard match with a win. 👀 pic.twitter.com/PCp4BwiqnH

Midway through the season, Chicago Fire made the decision to sell MLS top scorer Hugo Cuypers and acquire Robert Lewandowski. That move is starting to pay dividends: after six goalless matches, Lewandowski bagged a goal and an assist at Colorado Rapids before scoring two penalties vs. Columbus.

But it’s one thing to sign one of the greatest strikers of the 21st century. It’s another to back him up with a cohesive defensive unit. Chicago are struggling to find that balance, having failed to keep a clean sheet in their last eight matches and having conceded 10 goals in their last four.

Charlotte will be looking to build on their attacking momentum and exploit Chicago’s defensive frailties, having scored 11 goals in their last three outings. We're backing Charlotte to prevail in three and come away with their first-ever playoff series victory.

Can Antoine Griezmann lead Orlando to victory in Cincinnati? / Mike Stobe/MLS/Getty ImagesLast year, Orlando City finished ninth in the Eastern Conference and lost 3–1 at Chicago in the wild card match. They find themselves in danger of repeating that fate this year, with the Lions set to face a resurgent Cincinnati side that has taken 10 points from their last five outings.

Despite bringing in Antoine Griezmann midway through the campaign, Orlando have failed to secure an automatic playoff berth due in large part to their underwhelming form on the road. They’ve won three, drawn four, and lost 10 away from home, conceding 3.29 goals per away match. The last time they traveled to Cincinnati, they lost 6–2.
There’s only so much that Griezmann can do to paper over the cracks.
